analysis:
The two changed files are offline CI test scripts: scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py and scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py. No provider runtime, coordinator protocol, key custody, attestation, cache storage or authorization code is touched, so I found no regression against the TB-002/TB-003/TB-007/TB-009/TB-011/TB-012 assets or T-041.

The PR removes the console lane and its tests (console classification, lint-console route lane, retained console fixtures). The test-darkbloom-route.py head still pins workflow security properties: routed jobs get read-only permissions with no id-token or secrets, the router has empty permissions, release and credentialed workflows keep literal blacksmith runners, forks never contact the plane, https is required, and plane text cannot inject workflow commands. In scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py (head lines 203-218) the checks still forbid secrets, environment, id-token and repository in the public workflows. The detector test (lines 241-251) still requires fetch-depth 0, persist-credentials false and no pull_request_target. The provider aggregate gate truth table (lines 253-274) still fails closed unless the detector succeeded.

Two things to verify in integration. First, the base test_router_accepts_every_caller_configuration derives expectations from the ROUTED dict, and ci.yml must actually drop the lint-console job and console output. Those workflow and classifier changes (scripts/ci-component-paths.py, ci.yml, component-changes.yml) are outside this batch, so I could not check them. If they are left behind, test_every_workflow_is_classified or the lane checks would fail rather than weaken a control. Second, the test now treats console-ui/package-lock.json as selecting nothing. If console-ui remains in the repo and still has CI, that is a coverage decision rather than a provider-boundary issue. The head version of test-darkbloom-route.py was not supplied as a full file, only the patch, so the line-level checks rely on the base text plus the patch hunks. Nothing found suggests weakened test assertions on provider-sensitive paths.
